A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChatHLS, with matching methods, datasets and experiments. All pages, figures, tables and equations are readable and support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original results from 612 debugging cases, HLSFixer ablations and hardware synthesis evaluations on five computation kernels.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports additional optimizer comparisons and energy-efficiency proxy results.

M1.justification: The VODA/BugRAG construction, SFT/DPO HLSFixer with multi-agent fallback, and QoR-guided HLSTuner refinement remain. V2 clarifies golden-result verification and training-agent roles without establishing a changed algorithm. The omitted DeepSeek-R1 disclosure does not establish a model replacement.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training-corpus sizes, 612 debugging cases from the Kernel/Vitis/Manual groups, and five PolyBench optimization kernels. The additional comparisons and efficiency metric use this existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds RALAD to the optimization comparison in Figure 9 and HGBO-DSE to the DSL comparison in Figure 10. These extend the evaluated comparators to retrieval-augmented and learning-based optimizers, substantially broadening the comparison scope. Debugging comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds an Energy Efficiency proxy combining latency and resource utilization. Training budgets, synthesis tool/platform and iteration limits remain. V2 also omits v1's explicit latency/resource conditions for successful debugging; this reduces protocol specificity without establishing that testing changed.

E4.justification: The HLSFixer component ablation and 24-error-type analysis retain their designs and findings, including the 8.7%, 1.8% and 8.5% increments. Representative dynamic-allocation and DATAFLOW examples remain covered. The added efficiency scores do not introduce a separate ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both use point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds RALAD and HGBO-DSE results, including reported advantages of 2.5× and 1.4×, and the multi-method proxy results in Figure 11. It removes v1 Table III's detailed resource-cost results. Existing debugging rates and HLSTuner speedup values remain; the headline 4.9× to 3.6× change uses an expanded comparator set.

T1.justification: V2 introduces the nonlinear composite metric in Equation 2, using a latency activation function, resource penalties and sensitivity parameter gamma. It also removes v1's formal latency/resource conditions for repair success. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central ChatHLS, VODA, HLSFixer and HLSTuner contributions and 82.7% repair claim remain. The headline optimization claim changes from 4.9× against DSL approaches to 3.6× against DSL and learning-based approaches, revising its comparative scope.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explicit limitation that HLSTuner is less resource-efficient than Allo and ScaleHLS, alongside detailed DSL trade-off discussion. It adds an argument that the five kernels' structural patterns suffice to indicate strong generalization potential.

D1.justification: V2 corrects the swapped training-agent descriptions and adds golden-testbench and suggestion-scoring details. It removes identification of DeepSeek-R1 for the stronger optimization comparison, manual DSL-configuration information and benchmark URLs. Most numerical training and synthesis settings remain disclosed.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially recast. V2 adds HGBO-DSE, AutoDSE, hierarchical mixture-of-experts and retrieval-reasoning references, while removing C2HLSC, CodeRAG-Bench and the discussion contrasting VODA with prior iteratively refined HLS bug-injection datasets. These changes extend beyond bibliographic restyling.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method/evaluation prose are extensively condensed and rewritten. Background becomes Related Work, new training and comparison subheadings reorganize the narrative, and contributions are consolidated. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: V2 comprehensively reformats the document, adds bottleneck Figure 1 and efficiency Figure 11, and redraws optimization charts with additional series. It redesigns BugRAG Table 1, simplifies the baseline table and removes the resource-cost table. Existing figures are also relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens comparison coverage with RALAD and HGBO-DSE and clarifies training descriptions. However, it removes the DeepSeek-R1 configuration disclosure, detailed resource results and an explicit resource-efficiency limitation. The new efficiency proxy also leaves gamma unspecified. These gains in comparison breadth and losses in reproducibility and qualification prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
